Question: Which Microsoft 365 admin center is the BEST starting place to manage organization-wide settings such as custom domain names, release preferences, and service health?
Explanation 1: Microsoft 365 admin center is correct — the home for org settings, domains, release preferences, and tenant-wide service health.
Explanation 2: Exchange admin center is for Exchange Online mailboxes and groups.
Explanation 3: SharePoint admin center is for sites, libraries, and SharePoint settings.
Explanation 4: Teams admin center is for teams, channels, and Teams policies.
Overall Explanation: Microsoft 365 admin center is the correct answer because it is the home for organization-wide settings such as custom domain names, release preferences, and service health. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/admin-overview/admin-center
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: An admin needs to add a new custom domain name (e.g. contoso.com) to the Microsoft 365 tenant. Which admin center is the BEST place to perform this task?
Explanation 1: Microsoft 365 admin center is correct — domains are managed in Settings > Domains.
Explanation 2: Exchange admin center manages accepted domains for mail flow, but the primary domain management is in the M365 admin center.
Explanation 3: Microsoft Entra admin center manages custom domain names for the identity directory, but the recommended starting place for tenant-wide custom domain configuration is the M365 admin center.
Explanation 4: SharePoint admin center is for SharePoint.
Overall Explanation: Microsoft 365 admin center is the correct answer because custom domain names are managed in Settings > Domains in the M365 admin center. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/setup/add-domain
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which M365 admin center setting controls whether new features are released to users as soon as Microsoft rolls them out, or only after standard release validation?
Answer Option 1: Release preferences in the M365 admin center
Explanation 1: Release preferences in the M365 admin center is correct — it controls Targeted release vs Standard release for the entire tenant.
Answer Option 2: Standard release in Exchange admin center
Explanation 2: There is no 'Standard release' toggle in the Exchange admin center.
Answer Option 3: Update rings in the Teams admin center
Explanation 3: Update rings in Teams are for Teams app versions, not M365-wide feature release.
Answer Option 4: Service update settings in SharePoint admin center
Explanation 4: Service update settings in SharePoint are for SharePoint, not M365-wide.
Overall Explanation: Release preferences in the M365 admin center is the correct answer because it controls Targeted release vs Standard release for the entire tenant. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/release-options-in-office-365
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: An admin needs to verify that a user has the correct Microsoft 365 license assigned so they can use Exchange Online, SharePoint, and Teams. Which admin center is the BEST place to check user license assignments?
Answer Option 1: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users
Explanation 1: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users is correct — shows licenses, status, and sign-in info for each user.
Explanation 2: Exchange admin center > Recipients shows mailboxes but not full license info.
Explanation 3: SharePoint admin center > User profiles is for SharePoint profile properties.
Answer Option 4: Microsoft Entra admin center > Groups only
Explanation 4: Microsoft Entra admin center > Groups shows group memberships, not all user licenses.
Overall Explanation: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users is the correct answer because it shows each user's licenses, sign-in status, and assigned services. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which license type in Microsoft 365 typically grants a user access to Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, and the Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise desktop client?
Explanation 1: Microsoft 365 E3 (or equivalent) is correct — bundles Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, and the Office apps.
Explanation 2: Exchange Online Plan 1 only gives mail + basic features, not Teams or SharePoint.
Explanation 3: SharePoint Online Plan 1 only gives SharePoint, not Exchange or Teams.
Answer Option 4: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps standalone
Explanation 4: Defender for Cloud Apps standalone is a security add-on, not a productivity license.
Overall Explanation: Microsoft 365 E3 (or equivalent) is the correct answer because Microsoft 365 E3 bundles Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, and the Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise desktop client. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/commerce/licenses/plan-changes-and-license-updates
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: When you assign a Microsoft 365 license to a security group, what happens to the license assignment for new users added to that group?
Explanation 1: They automatically inherit the license — group-based licensing assigns and removes licenses based on group membership.
Answer Option 2: You must manually assign the license to each new user
Explanation 2: Manual per-user assignment is not required when using group-based licensing.
Answer Option 3: The license is blocked for group-based users
Explanation 3: Group-based licensing is fully supported.
Answer Option 4: Group-based licensing is not supported in Microsoft 365
Explanation 4: Group-based licensing is supported.
Overall Explanation: They automatically inherit the license is the correct answer because group-based licensing in Microsoft 365 automatically assigns and removes licenses based on group membership. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/licensing/licensing-groups-assign
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which M365 feature lets an organization schedule a regular, automatic license assignment to new users in a particular department by using group membership?
Explanation 1: Group-based licensing is correct — assign a license to a group and members inherit it.
Explanation 2: Direct user assignment is one-by-one.
Explanation 3: Conditional Access enforces authentication policy, not license assignment.
Explanation 4: Azure Policy enforces resource configuration, not license assignment.
Overall Explanation: Group-based licensing is the correct answer because group-based licensing automatically assigns and removes licenses based on group membership. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/licensing/licensing-groups-assign
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which of the following objects can a Microsoft 365 license be assigned to? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: An individual user — true. Direct user assignment is supported.
Explanation 2: A security group — true. Group-based licensing works with security groups.
Explanation 3: A Microsoft 365 group — true. Group-based licensing works with Microsoft 365 groups.
Explanation 4: A distribution group — false. Distribution groups (mail-only) do not support license assignment.
Overall Explanation: An individual user, a security group, and a Microsoft 365 group can all receive a license assignment. Distribution groups (mail-only) do not support license assignment. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/licensing/licensing-groups-assign
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which admin center is the BEST place to manage Exchange Online mailboxes, distribution groups, and mail flow rules?

Explanation 4: Teams admin center is for Teams.

Question: Which object in the Exchange admin center represents a single mailbox-enabled recipient (user, shared mailbox, or resource) that can send and receive email?

Explanation 4: Team is a Teams object.

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Exchange object is BEST for sending email to a list of recipients without requiring each recipient to have an Exchange Online license?

Explanation 3: Shared mailbox requires a license to enable.
Explanation 4: Resource mailbox is for room/equipment, not mailing lists.

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Exchange Online mailbox type is BEST for a shared inbox that multiple users can access (e.g. info@contoso.com) without giving one user a personal mailbox?

Explanation 3: Resource mailbox is for rooms/equipment.
Explanation 4: Linked mailbox is for on-premises synced accounts.
Overall Explanation: Shared mailbox is the correct answer because a shared mailbox allows multiple users to access a common inbox without giving one user a personal mailbox. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/email/create-a-shared-mailbox
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which admin center is the BEST place to manage SharePoint site collections, site-level sharing settings, and access control policies?
Explanation 1: Microsoft 365 admin center is the tenant home, not the focused SharePoint tool.

Explanation 3: SharePoint admin center is correct — focused tool for site collections and sharing settings.
Explanation 4: Teams admin center is for Teams.

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: What is a SharePoint site collection?
Answer Option 1: A single document in a library
Explanation 1: A single document is a file, not a container.
Answer Option 2: A top-level container that holds sites, lists, libraries, and content
Explanation 2: A top-level container that holds sites, lists, libraries, and content is correct.
Explanation 3: Teams chat is for chat, not storage.
Explanation 4: Mailbox is mail.
Overall Explanation: A top-level container that holds sites, lists, libraries, and content is the correct answer because a SharePoint site collection is a top-level organizational container for all SharePoint content. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/sites/site-collections
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: What is a SharePoint library?
Answer Option 1: A collection of documents and files within a site
Explanation 1: A collection of documents and files within a site is correct — a library is where documents live and are versioned.
Explanation 2: A list of users is a SharePoint group or directory object.
Explanation 3: A Teams channel is for chat.
Explanation 4: An Exchange folder is for mail.
Overall Explanation: A collection of documents and files within a site is the correct answer because a SharePoint library is a document container within a site that supports versioning, metadata, and co-authoring. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/intro-to-libraries
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which SharePoint role provides FULL control over a site, including the ability to manage permissions, add users, and change site settings?
Explanation 1: Site visitor is read-only.
Explanation 2: Site member can edit content but not manage site settings.
Explanation 3: Site owner is correct — full control over the site.
Explanation 4: Site reader is read-only.
Overall Explanation: Site owner is the correct answer because the site owner role provides full control over a site, including the ability to manage permissions, add users, and change site settings. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/modern-experience-sharing-permissions
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which of the following are SharePoint permission roles for a site? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Site owner — true. Full control over the site.
Explanation 2: Site member — true. Can edit content but not change site settings.
Explanation 3: Site visitor — true. Read-only access.
Explanation 4: Site auditor — false. This is not a standard SharePoint site role (Microsoft Purview eDiscovery has an Auditor concept, but not in SharePoint).

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which admin center is the BEST place to manage Microsoft Teams settings, including Teams policies, calling policies, and meeting policies?
Explanation 1: M365 admin center is the tenant home, not the focused Teams tool.

Explanation 3: SharePoint admin center is for SharePoint.
Explanation 4: Teams admin center is correct — focused tool for Teams settings and policies.
Overall Explanation: Teams admin center is the correct answer because the Teams admin center is the focused tool for Teams settings, Teams policies, calling policies, and meeting policies. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-teams-in-modern-portal
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: In Microsoft Teams, what is a channel?
Explanation 1: A single chat message is a message, not a channel.

Explanation 4: Site collection is SharePoint.

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Teams policy is BEST used to control who can create new teams in your Microsoft 365 tenant?

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Microsoft Entra ID feature is the default identity provider for Microsoft 365, storing users, groups, devices, and application identities?

Explanation 3: B2C is for customer identity.
Explanation 4: External ID (B2B) is for partner users.

Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which authentication method requires users to provide two or more authentication factors (password + phone code) to sign in?
Explanation 1: SSO lets users use one identity, but does not require multiple factors.
Explanation 2: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is correct — requires two or more factors.
Explanation 3: Conditional Access is a policy engine, not a factor check itself.
Explanation 4: Passwordless removes passwords entirely, not multiple factors.
Overall Explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is the correct answer because MFA requires two or more authentication factors (something you know, have, or are). Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mfa-howitworks
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Microsoft Entra feature is the policy engine that evaluates signals (user, device, location, risk) to enforce access decisions like requiring MFA or blocking sign-in?
Explanation 1: MFA is the factor check, not the policy engine.
Explanation 2: Conditional Access is correct — the policy engine that evaluates signals and enforces decisions.
Explanation 3: PIM is for time-bound role activation.
Explanation 4: Identity Protection generates risk signals.
Overall Explanation: Conditional Access is the correct answer because Conditional Access is the policy engine that evaluates signals (user, device, location, risk) and enforces access decisions. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/overview
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Microsoft Entra feature allows a user to authenticate ONCE with a single set of credentials to access multiple Microsoft 365 and SaaS applications?
Explanation 1: MFA is multi-factor authentication, not single sign-on.
Explanation 2: Single sign-on (SSO) is correct — authenticate once and access many apps.
Explanation 3: Conditional Access is a policy engine.
Explanation 4: Identity Protection generates risk signals.
Overall Explanation: Single sign-on (SSO) is the correct answer because SSO allows a user to authenticate once with a single set of credentials to access multiple applications. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/SSO/overview
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Microsoft Entra feature provides just-in-time, time-bound, approval-based activation of privileged roles?
Explanation 1: Conditional Access is a policy engine.
Explanation 2: MFA is an authentication factor check.
Explanation 3: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is correct — just-in-time, time-bound, approval-based role activation.
Explanation 4: Access Reviews are periodic attestation.
Overall Explanation: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is the correct answer because PIM provides just-in-time, time-bound, approval-based activation of privileged roles. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Zero Trust principle states 'never trust, always verify' for every access request?
Explanation 1: Defense in depth is a layered-security model.
Explanation 2: Verify explicitly is correct — authenticate and authorize every access request based on all available signals.
Explanation 3: Least privilege is a separate principle.
Explanation 4: Assume breach is another principle.
Overall Explanation: Verify explicitly is the correct answer because Zero Trust's verify-explicitly principle requires authenticating and authorizing every access request based on all available signals. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Zero Trust principle recommends granting only the access needed to perform the task?
Explanation 1: Verify explicitly is a different principle.
Explanation 2: Least privilege access is correct — grant only the access needed.
Explanation 3: Assume breach is a different principle.
Explanation 4: Defense in depth is a different model.
Overall Explanation: Least privilege access is the correct answer because Zero Trust's least-privilege-access principle recommends granting only the access needed. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview
Domain: Identify the Core Features and Objects of Microsoft 365 Services

Question: Which Microsoft 365 audit log records subscription-level administrative events (create, update, delete, role assignment) for auditing?

Question: Which Microsoft Defender XDR component is BEST for visibility, control, and threat protection for SaaS applications (Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Google Workspace)?
